noah: quick idea drop 10 thinking about a 'regional control relay' model inside customer VPCs: a small HA relay pair per region that handles control-plane mTLS and optional egress SNAT. Spokes (agents) would be thin and only talk to local relay. Pros: single peering per region, centralized observability. Cons: relay blast radius + egress cost concentration.

emma: question 10 does relay terminate control mTLS or pass through? if it terminates we can do auth checks and routing, but customers with strict compliance may want passthrough to their host.

noah: plan is to terminate control mTLS at the relay for auth and routing, but support data-path passthrough for model traffic when requested (SNI/TCP). We'll also support a "preserve_source_ip" mode via TPROXY on relays if customer allows kernel tweaks.

jules: ops note 10 relays must be active-active across AZs and have health-based route preferences. spokes should randomize failover backoff to avoid bursts. Also need canary ACL rollouts to avoid mass-blackholes.

ops-sre: add metrics: per-relay bandwidth, NAT gateway bytes, per-tenant egress IP mapping errors, and probe for cross-relay failover time. We should spike with: (A) default relay SNAT path, (B) relay TPROXY hairpin, (C) dedicated per-tenant endpoint.

sec: security checklist 10 KMS integration for any keys on relay, threat model for terminating mTLS in customer VPC, and proof that passthrough mode preserves E2E integrity.

noah: spike owners: jules (infra), emma (security), ops-sre (runbooks). Success criteria: handshake p95 <100ms, failover <45s, and egress cost delta within 20% for small tenants.

deploy-bot: scheduled spike-job (id: spike-2026-03-10-relay-pattern) :rocket:

emma: OK let's run the spike and we can follow with an RFC including diagrams and a rollback playbook. :thumbsup:
